name: Priit Mihkelson Turtle Defense System
description: Navigate Priit Mihkelson's Protecting & Generating Dynamic Offense From The Turtle by separating posture, specific attacking threats and exits.
summary: Priit Mihkelson's turtle course organizes posture and threat responses before presenting routes back to guard or standing.
overview: Choose this material when your difficult exchange begins in turtle. The outline lets you distinguish an early posture question from a hook, harness or choke problem, then locate an exit destination instead of treating remaining in turtle as the entire objective.

products.title: Protecting & Generating Dynamic Offense From The Turtle
products.blurb: Four volumes progress from turtle posture and specific threats to guard-return and standing options.
products.best_for: Practitioners whose study problem begins in turtle and who want to identify both the attack and an exit destination.
products.study_focus: Start with Volume 1, Turtle Posture (8:33); compare the later threat-specific lesson with the relevant exit in Volume 4.

guide.display_title: Priit Mihkelson: Turtle Defense and Exits

fits: You repeatedly reach turtle and want to separate posture study from responses to a particular attack.
You want to compare returning to guard with standing from turtle.
consider_alternative_if: You are already held in rear mount: Back Defense Protocol points to Brian Glick's separate overhook-side, underhook-side and body-triangle sections.

includes: Volume 1 lists posture, neck and elbow topics, resistance to pushing and pulling, and hooks.
Volumes 2–3 address harnesses, clock chokes, passing situations, wrestling tilts, front-headlock submissions and crucifix threats.
Volume 4 moves from hip-pull and harness responses to spin escapes, guard returns, Granby movement and standing.
limits: The course is organized around turtle; established rear-mount escapes have a more direct study route in the Glick companion.
The published lesson names distinguish threats and exits but do not explain the posture adjustments or movements.

start_here.title: Separate the turtle threat from the exit destination
start_here.task: Choose a turtle exchange from your own footage or notes. Name the attack you can actually identify, then choose which destination you wanted: guard or standing. Find that threat in Volumes 2–3 and compare the guard-return and standing entries in Volume 4. If the attack is unclear, start your course study at Turtle Posture and record what the instructor uses to distinguish the situations before selecting a later lesson.
start_here.section: Volume 1: Turtle Posture (8:33–12:57); Volume 4: Shin Frame Spin to Guard (20:06–22:13) and Standing from Turtle (30:08–34:16)
